newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-UNITED FAVOURITES TO WIN CLASH OF GIANTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-UNITED FAVOURITES TO WIN CLASH OF GIANTS.

text.p: The only thing that points to a Tottenham victory when they travel to Old Trafford for their third round F.A. Cup match against Manchester United on Sunday is past history. On current form, United look home and dry.

Upsets have happened throughout the long and dramatic history of the F.A. Cup and a Tottenham win over United would be a mild surprise compared to some of those seen since 1871 when the competition began.

But following their 6-1 defeat in the League Cup to Bolton, their 7-1 defeat at Newcastle last Saturday and their generally indifferent form, Tottenham do not look to have too much chance against the Cup holders.

United played some of their best football of the season during the busy Christmas period, beating Sunderland 5-0, Nottingham Forest 4-0 and Leeds 1-0 before being held to a 0-0 draw by Aston Villa on Wednesday night.

In contrast, Tottenham drew 1-1 with Sheffield Wednesday, beat lowly Southampton 3-1 and were then crushed at Newcastle, suggesting another season at White Hart Lane will end in disappointment and frustration.
Realistically, the only trophy Spurs can still get their hands on is the F.A. Cup and if they lose to United their season is over -- barring the annual scramble for a UEFA Cup place.

Manager Gerry Francis has strengthened his squad recently with the 2.6 million pound ($4.4 million) signing of defender John Scales from Liverpool and 20-year-old Norwegian striker Steffen Iversen, who cost 2.0 million pounds ($3.4 million) from Rosenborg.
But the lack of a creative midfielder is at the heart of Spurs' problems. Too much of their approach play is too predictable.

On Sunday manager Gerry Francis will get a first-hand view of exactly what it is that his side lacks when he sees Ryan Giggs, David Beckham, Roy Keane and Eric Cantona try to create their habitual space, time and magic in the United midfield.

Despite Tottenham's indifferent league form, they have traditionally saved their best football for the F.A. Cup. Spurs have only won the English title twice, but their eight Cup wins set a record they shared with United until last season when Alex Ferguson's men brought the trophy back to Old Trafford for the ninth time.
Tottenham have always been known as "a cup team" and will have to tap into some kind of collective inspirational memory if they are to raise their game from the mediocrity of much of this season.

In 12 previous F.A. Cup meetings against United, Tottenham have won five times, five matches have been drawn and United have won twice. Spurs won 1-0 on their last visit to Old Trafford in the Cup in 1980 with an Ossie Ardiles goal in the last minute of extra time. They will need something out of the ordinary to succeed again.

For their part, United have not only bettered Tottenham's all-time F.A. Cup-winning record, they have also eclipsed Spurs' double-winning performance of 1961 by winning the league and cup double twice in the last three seasons.
They are now bidding to become the first club to reach four successive F.A. Cup finals after defeating Chelsea in 1994, losing to Everton in 1995 and beating Liverpool last season.
At least six matches stand between them and another Wembley appearance but by Sunday night United will probably have overcome the first obstacle -- no matter that the omens are on Tottenham's side.

Manchester United (from): Peter Schmeichel; Gary Neville, David May, Ronnie Johnsen, Denis Irwin, David Beckham, Nicky Butt, Roy Keane, Ryan Giggs, Eric Cantona, Ole Solskjaer, Andy Cole, Brian McClair, Karel Poborsky

Tottenham (from): Ian Walker; Colin Calderwood, Sol Campbell, Clive Wilson, John Scales, Stephen Carr, Andy Sinton, David Howells, Ruel Fox, Andy Sinton, Allan Nielsen, Teddy Sheringham, Steffen Iversen, Jason Dozzell
